judgement_details.explanation: The response states: 'If your confidence interval is higher, the more reliable your results can be which will affect how businesses make their financial decisions.' This is misleading. According to reference [19], a higher confidence level (e.g., 99% vs 95%) results in a wider confidence interval, which reflects greater uncertainty, not greater reliability in the precision of the estimate. While the interval is more likely to contain the true value, it is less precise. Thus, higher confidence does not equate to more reliable or better results—it trades precision for increased certainty. This misrepresents the trade-off inherent in confidence intervals.
